t: This is the place where the bronze statue of Robert Stephenson usually stands, on a red granite plinth in the forecourt of Euston station. It's currently not here. It was removed in 2020 to make way for the High Speed 2 rebuilding of the station, and was installed at the Locomotion Museum in Shildon, County Durham, in 2025. Carlo Marochetti, the Italian-born sculptor, made it, and it was erected in 1871. Stephenson was a railway engineer and the only son of George Stephenson, the Father of Railways. The statue was one of the few surviving parts of the original station.
